headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risk from browser/MCP-enabled support agent feeding Superset; no direct shared-channel evidence, so uncertainty is elevated.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A can run browsers and use runtime-injected MCPs/hooks, so it may ingest untrusted content; Agent B exposes only a Superset API, so the pairwise bridge is inferred rather than documented. Because no shared channel is proven, I choose medium over low under the uncertainty rule.
conditions: IF agent_a browser output or MCP content is copied into agent_b inputs without sanitization
IF a shared filesystem or message bridge is configured between the two agents
mitigations: Disable browser-to-agent handoff for untrusted pages
Require provenance tags on any content passed from A to B
Use a read-only staging folder for inter-agent artifacts
Turn off runtime-injected MCPs unless needed
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and allowlist parsing

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A touches session history, project code, and provider auth data, while Agent B has allowlisted network egress and a Superset API surface. If A’s files or prompts are forwarded into B, sensitive material could leave the local boundary; the shared-workspace path is not documented, so this is inferred and escalated conservatively.
conditions: IF agent_a session history or provider auth data is passed into agent_b requests
IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace containing secrets
mitigations: Remove secrets from any shared workspace before running B
Restrict B to non-sensitive datasets only
Rotate provider credentials if A has handled them
Use separate OS users or containers for each agent
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A has broad network egress and subprocess spawning; Agent B has allowlisted egress and only a Superset API. There is no evidence of overlapping write access, git state, or shared mutable resources, so a direct capability conflict is not established and remains low.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same directory or database
IF an orchestrator maps both agents onto the same mutable OAuth or API scope
mitigations: Assign separate workspaces
Avoid shared credentials
Serialize any writes through one agent
Check for overlapping API scopes before deployment

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A can generate browser-derived or tool-derived content, and Agent B can act on Superset API inputs. If B treats A’s output as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect analytics actions; this pathway is plausible but not directly evidenced, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes agent_a output without verification
IF agent_a produces instructions or facts that B uses to call the Superset API
mitigations: Insert a human review step before B acts
Require schema validation on A’s outputs
Log and diff A-to-B handoffs
Limit B to read-only Superset operations
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: Agent A handles provider auth prompts, installation identifiers, and session history, while Agent B lists no sensitive data classes or special compliance claims. No residency or certification mismatch is documented, so only a low compliance concern remains from A’s sensitive handling surface.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into agent_a prompts or session history
IF agent_b is later used to process the same regulated data class
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of A’s prompts
Document retention for session history
Use separate environments for regulated workloads
Review vendor compliance before enabling sensitive datasets
